verses.text: In the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah's rule, Sennacherib king of Assyria attacked all the walled cities of Judah and captured them.

Then the king of Assyria sent his field commander from Lachish to King Hezekiah in Jerusalem with a large army. The commander stood by the water channel of the upper pool, on the road to the washerman's field.
Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was in charge of the palace, Shebna the secretary, and Joah son of Asaph, the record keeper, went out to meet him.
The field commander said to them, "Tell Hezekiah: 'This is what the great king, the king of Assyria, says: What are you trusting in that makes you so confident?
You say you have a plan and strength for war, but those are only empty words. Who are you depending on, that you dare to rebel against me?

Look, you are trusting in Egypt, that broken reed of a walking stick. If a man leans on it, it will cut into his hand and pierce it. That is what Pharaoh king of Egypt is like to all who trust in him.
But if you say to me, "We trust in the LORD our God," is he not the one whose high places and altars Hezekiah removed? Hezekiah told Judah and Jerusalem, "You must worship before this one altar."
Now make a deal with my master, the king of Assyria. I will give you two thousand horses, if you can find enough riders to put on them!
How can you turn back even the weakest officer among my master's servants? Yet you trust in Egypt for chariots and horsemen!
Do you think I have come to attack and destroy this land without the LORD? The LORD himself told me, "Go up against this land and destroy it."'"

Then Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah said to the field commander, "Please speak to us, your servants, in Aramaic, because we understand it. Do not speak to us in Hebrew where the people on the wall can hear."

But the commander said, "Did my master send me to say these things only to your master and to you? Did he not also send me to the men sitting on the wall, who will have to eat their own dung and drink their own urine along with you?"
Then the commander stood and shouted loudly in Hebrew, "Listen to the words of the great king, the king of Assyria!
This is what the king says: 'Do not let Hezekiah fool you. He cannot rescue you.
Do not let Hezekiah make you trust in the LORD by saying, "The LORD will surely rescue us. This city will not be handed over to the king of Assyria."

Do not listen to Hezekiah. This is what the king of Assyria says: Make peace with me and come out to me. Then each of you will eat from your own vine and your own fig tree, and drink water from your own well,
until I come and take you away to a land like your own, a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards.
Do not let Hezekiah mislead you by saying, "The LORD will rescue us." Have the gods of any nation ever rescued their land from the hand of the king of Assyria?
Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim? Did they rescue Samaria from my hand?
Which of all the gods of these lands has ever rescued their land from me? So how can the LORD rescue Jerusalem from my hand?'"
But the people stayed silent and did not answer a word, because the king had commanded, "Do not answer him."

Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was in charge of the palace, Shebna the secretary, and Joah son of Asaph, the record keeper, went to Hezekiah with their clothes torn, and told him what the field commander had said.
